cases.title: Escape must close the suggestion list without erasing what the user typed
cases.summary: Pressing Escape to dismiss suggestions sets the input value to an empty string, so a user editing a saved field loses their text.
cases.status: Open. The maintainer tracks the change for v11 in issue #485; no fix is merged at pinnedCommit (the current head).

review.reviewer: Project review after the browser verdict, written with Claude Code (the AI assistant that built this project). A reading of the patch, not another test.
review.summary: Escape now only closes the list: the lines that emptied the input and emitted the clear event on Escape are removed, the behaviour the maintainer proposed in #485.
caveats: A page that listened for the clear event on Escape no longer receives it; #485 accepts that.
Ultra wrote it on the second attempt, after Super’s patch did not apply.

cases.expectedBehaviour: As proposed by the maintainer in #485: Escape closes the list only and keeps the input. The reporter of #402 suggested restoring the earlier value instead; this task follows the maintainer's plan.

cases.title: Passing through a prefilled datepicker must not change the date the form submits
cases.summary: The datepicker instance is created on focusin and immediately rewrites the input with a locale string, so a saved 2026-10-22 is submitted as 10/22/2026 although the user never picked a date.
cases.status: Open. Fixes are proposed in pull requests #43150 and #43151, not merged at pinnedCommit. They are never sent to the model.

pendingHumanCheck.applied: js/src changes only (tests and docs omitted)
pendingHumanCheck.note: The pending human fix passes the same frozen task. It was fetched for comparison and is never part of a model request.

review.reviewer: Project review after the browser verdict, written with Claude Code (the AI assistant that built this project). A reading of the patch, not another test.
review.verdict: Works, but not acceptable upstream as written
review.summary: For an input without a separate display element, the date formatter now returns YYYY-MM-DD before it looks at the dateFormat option, so focusing no longer rewrites a saved ISO value.
caveats: Every input datepicker now shows ISO dates and ignores a configured dateFormat, including a custom formatter function.
The pending human fixes keep the configured format and separate the displayed text from the submitted value; this patch does not.

The stricter case bootstrap6-datepicker-focus-rewrites-date-custom-format adds a datepicker with a long dateFormat. This patch fails it; seven of the ten earlier model patches and the pending human fix pass it.

cases.expectedBehaviour: Only the part of the issue every proposal agrees on: focusing and leaving the field without picking keeps the submitted value 2026-10-22. What a newly picked date should submit is still being decided upstream and is not tested.

cases.title: Tab must leave a datepicker input for the next field
cases.summary: When the field is reached with Tab, the calendar does not open, but vanilla-calendar-pro treats it as shown: on the next Tab it cancels the key and focuses the first control of a calendar that is not in the page, so focus stays in the date field. Escape is the only way out, and it drops focus to the page body.
cases.status: Found by Tabstitch and reported upstream as twbs/bootstrap#43202 on 2026-10-26 (reduced test case re-checked against the published 6.0.0-alpha.1 bundle and main at d793f282). Reproduced in headless Chromium 156 and desktop Chrome 155. A Bootstrap maintainer triaged it the same day, labelled confirmed, bug, accessibility and v6.

review.reviewer: Project review after the browser verdict, written with Claude Code (the AI assistant that built this project). A reading of the patch, not another test.
review.summary: A capture-phase Tab listener on the input hides the datepicker and stops the event before vanilla-calendar-pro can cancel it, so Tab leaves the field.
caveats: After a click opens the calendar, Tab now closes it and moves on instead of moving into the calendar, which is the designed behaviour.
stopPropagation hides every Tab keydown on the input from the page’s own bubbling listeners.
Reported upstream as twbs/bootstrap#43202; this patch is not proposed there.

cases.expectedBehaviour: With the calendar closed, Tab moves to the next field (WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap). When the calendar is open, for example after a click, Tab moving into it is the library's intended design and is not changed by this task. Escape keeps closing the calendar.

cases.title: A dialog created with keyboard: false must stay open however often Escape is pressed
cases.summary: keyboard: false only calls preventDefault() on the native cancel event. Escape does not count as user activation, so after a few presses Chromium fires cancel with cancelable=false and the dialog closes anyway.
cases.status: Open and labelled confirmed. A maintainer-side fix is proposed in pull request #43077, not merged at pinnedCommit. That pull request is never sent to the model; it is kept for comparison after it merges.

pendingHumanCheck.note: The pending human fix passes the same frozen task. It was fetched for comparison and is never part of a model request.

review.reviewer: Project review after the browser verdict, written with Claude Code (the AI assistant that built this project). A reading of the patch, not another test.
review.verdict: Rejected on review: breaks Escape for every default dialog
review.summary: The Escape keydown handler now runs for modal dialogs too and calls preventDefault() before it checks the keyboard option, so the keyboard: false dialog stays open, as the task requires.
caveats: An ordinary dialog with the default keyboard: true no longer closes on Escape either, checked in Chromium without inference. The frozen task had no such dialog.

The stricter case bootstrap6-dialog-escape-keyboard-false-default-dialog adds one with a guard. This patch fails it, while the four earlier model patches for this bug and the pending human fix (#43077) pass it.
It also removes the static-backdrop bounce that signals a dialog cannot be dismissed.

cases.title: Opening a drawer must move keyboard focus into it
cases.summary: A closed drawer is visibility: hidden and becomes visible through the slide-in transition. showModal() runs its focusing steps while everything inside is still hidden, so focus falls back to body and the trigger behind the modal is inert.
cases.status: Open, labelled confirmed and needs-decision. A fix is proposed in pull request #43139, not merged at pinnedCommit. That pull request is never sent to the model.

pendingHumanCheck.note: The pending human fix changes scss/_drawer.scss. This case serves the published 6.0.0-alpha.1 stylesheet, so the SCSS change was not compiled or checked here.

review.reviewer: Project review after the browser verdict, written with Claude Code (the AI assistant that built this project). A reading of the patch, not another test.
review.summary: After the drawer’s shown event, focus moves to the first focusable element inside it, so keyboard focus no longer falls back to the body.
caveats: The selector list does not prefer an [autofocus] element and does not skip disabled or hidden controls.
Focus moves only after the slide-in transition ends; the pending human fix in #43139 instead fixes the visibility timing so the native dialog focusing steps work.
The stricter case bootstrap6-drawer-initial-focus-autofocus puts an [autofocus] field in the drawer. This patch and both earlier passing patches fail it.

cases.expectedBehaviour: Focus lands on the first focusable control in the drawer, its close button, as for a native modal dialog. The compiled stylesheet is a dependency outside the editable source, so a repair has to be made in the TypeScript.

cases.title: Arrow keys must not select a day that disableDayFn closes
cases.summary: A disabled day cannot be clicked, but ArrowRight from Friday selects the closed Saturday and the form submits it.
cases.status: Open since July 2025 and confirmed by a second user. The repository was archived, so no upstream fix will ship.

review.reviewer: Project review after the browser verdict, written with Claude Code (the AI assistant that built this project). A reading of the patch, not another test.
review.verdict: Rejected on review: hangs at maxDate
review.summary: Arrow keys now step past days that minDate, maxDate, disableWeekends or disableDayFn close, instead of selecting them.
caveats: At a range boundary the do…while loop never finds an allowed date: with a maxDate set, ArrowRight on that day hung the page in Chromium, while the unpatched library stayed on the day.
The stricter case pikaday-keyboard-disabled-day-max-date adds a maxDate and a guard. This patch fails it, while the three earlier model patches for this bug pass it.
It keeps Pikaday’s own 24-hour millisecond steps, which can land on the wrong day across a daylight-saving change (a separate flaw that the original adjustDate shares).

cases.expectedBehaviour: Author decision: the arrow key moves to the next day that is not disabled, as when a user skips over closed days with the pointer.

cases.title: Tab after typing a date must move to the next field, not jump back into the date field
cases.summary: Typing a date and pressing Tab fires change; Pikaday redraws and, one millisecond later, focuses the date field again, so the next field loses focus and the user's typing lands in the wrong place.
cases.status: Open since January 2019. The repository was archived, so no upstream fix will ship.

review.reviewer: Project review after the browser verdict, written with Claude Code (the AI assistant that built this project). A reading of the patch, not another test.
review.summary: The patch removes the timer that refocused the date field one millisecond after every redraw, which is what pulled focus back after Tab. A reviewer probe of the mouse paths the task does not cover (open by click, Next month, type, pick a day) gives the same focus and value with and without the patch.
caveats: The refocus is removed for every redraw, not only the one after change. The probe covered mouse navigation in desktop Chromium; touch devices were not tested.
Pikaday is archived, so this is a patch for teams that vendor it, not an upstream pull request.
